The Sabin Vaccine Institute announced it has completed enrollment in all six Phase 2 clinical trials for its cAd3-Marburg Vaccine and its cAd3-Sudan Ebolavirus Vaccine candidates.  There are no licensed vaccines for protection against disease caused by Marburg virus or the Sudan virus strain of Ebola. Both are highly contagious hemorrhagic fever diseases that can have a high fatality rate of up to 88%.    Phase 2 clinical trials to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of the two monovalent vaccines, both on the cAd3 platform, began in healthy volunteers in Africa in 2023 and in the United States in 2025. The African trials, with sites in Kenya and Uganda, completed participant follow-up last year and reporting activities are progressing. The U.S. trials completed enrollment last month.  In addition, Sabin’s cAd3-Marburg Vaccine has been used in Phase 2 rapid response outbreak clinical trials in Africa — more than 1,700 participants enrolled in 2024 during an outbreak in Rwanda, and more than 500 participants enrolled beginning last December for Ethiopia’s first-ever Marburg outbreak.   Learn more ⤵️  https://ow.ly/K19e50YrNbg

Partners in the #GlobalHPVConsortium work with local organizations every day to #EliminateCervicalCancer and #PreventHPV. Here, VillageReach takes over our account with #SocialWithSabin as part of #CervicalCancerAwarenessMonth, sharing a success story from #Nigeria ⤵️  --  Enugu has stood out as a top performer among all South-Eastern Nigerian states in driving HPV vaccine uptake, with 99% coverage as of October 2025, and our partners at the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) have recognized the progress there, especially around key efforts like Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (MNCH) Weeks.  🔥 How we did it:  Townhall-style dialogues brought people together — moms, teachers, chiefs, religious leaders, and young people — to talk honestly about HPV and the vaccine, where questions were welcomed and fears were respectfully unpacked through:  ✨ Trust: Health workers broke down the science, teachers explained school delivery logistics, and local leaders tied health protection to family and faith. ✨ Action: Caregivers and adolescents who wanted the adolescent to receive the vaccine were linked to on-site vaccination teams. ✨ Partnership: Together with the NPHCDA and local health agencies, Enugu communities kept HPV vaccination visible and accessible, with state leadership setting the direction. We supported school-based delivery and church-based sensitization to build comfort and confidence about the HPV vaccine among girls and those around them. "Unlike COVID-19, there is no commercial market for a Marburg vaccine. Demand is limited to outbreak response, health workers, and emergency stockpiles. Progress depends almost entirely on public sector and philanthropic investment. Sabin’s role is to ensure that lack of commercial viability does not translate into lack of protection."  Sabin Vaccine Institute CEO Amy Finan reflects on a defining moment in 2025 — when #Ethiopia's Ministry of Health reached out for support as the country faced its first-ever outbreak of #Marburg virus disease.   Having responded to a Marburg outbreak in Rwanda the year before, the Sabin team moved quickly — building on established partnerships and lessons learned to support the national response, while generating evidence to support the development of our investigational cAd3-Marburg vaccine.  Read more ⤵️ https://www.sabin.org/resources/2025-spotlight-reflections-on-outbreak-response-and-generating-meaningful-data/   #OutbreakResponse
